notes: Cam rise is kinematic. From belt enable, a free torus responds to compliant tread contact, motor current, gravity and field surfaces. The held cassette starts both belts from rest. Air drag, actual friction and finished inertia remain unmeasured.

Free chassis on unilateral tire and bumper contacts. Twenty-four articulated chain links connect two field anchors. Two ideal gate constraints engage inside a 12 mm capture window. The pivot has a 215 N·m limit. Motor torque goes to zero at 4 s. The brake holds for the remaining 5 s.

Field meshes are reduced from FE-2024.STEP in its registered coordinates. The physics uses separate original speaker surfaces and a lumped chain. The colored opening outline marks the actual scoring plane.
Nominal foam compression is represented by the two rigid tread/NOTE overlaps. Six post reliefs clear the outer tread return. Baseline and failing trials are retained locally.

Drive screen uses 50 A motor limit per side, direct pulleys, 0.20 kg effective moving mass per belt and assumed grip. At the sensor-registered placement, the 0.18 and 0.22 kg cases also register. Moving the robot 120 mm downfield misses registration in the tested coarse run.

The ideal hook constraint starts from a chain within 12 mm of each throat. Gate capture from a driving approach, clearance to every truss member, air drag and drive hardware are open. The suspended chassis continues swinging during the disabled interval.

Shovel stock is nominally 3.0 mm above the flat carpet. Swing bumper clearance bound 85.2 mm; front reach bound 642.3 mm against the 644.8 mm project envelope. Up to 21.3 mm extra slide retraction. Complete truck support, fasteners, wear and loaded flex remain open.
The shaft moved 58 mm toward the mouth and 12 mm above the old axis. The raised ends of both lid rails support it. The spring and stop are preliminary parameters.
Profile A is the default. At fixed pivot height, 0.384° of extra nose-down pitch uses the nominal 3.0 mm floor clearance. Measure loaded pitch, wear and carpet variation on the physical nose.

Bounded risk experiment 01. The staged shot scored on both numerical refinements. The raised stop traded reduced digging for a missed high-side pickup. The finite friction brake slipped at all three CG positions. The five Trial replays use the same assembled robot.

Catch stock, fasteners and actuator reserve add 0.263–0.453 kg. A 2 A peak allowance is included in the electrical ledger. Rigid dog contact was verified against the modeled normal face; a 1° overrotation enters it. Earlier angular-spring trials are retained as controls.
focus: The indexed scorer missed a required count on each of the first two varied setups. Select R01 or R02 to see the floor pickup, loaded return and field rebound.

objectives.objective: Acquire and retain a loose floor NOTE
objectives.basis: Two passive floor followers maintained the tested pickup band across 72 parameter combinations. Actual carpet, wheel wear and arm loading need calibration.

objectives.objective: Score six distinct floor NOTES in 120 seconds on 19 of 20 frozen starts
objectives.basis: Nominal fine replay scored six in 115.07 s. R01 and R02 both missed a required sensor event after full opening passage. With 18 starts remaining, this controller cannot reach 19/20.

objectives.objective: Turn and raise while carrying; recover or reset for the next pickup
objectives.basis: The floor NOTE stayed in the cassette through the commanded swing and slide at both resolutions. Traversal under chassis acceleration and yaw is open.

The disabled-hold model started with ideal gated points. The original closed keepers intersect the as-installed FIRST chain by 188.0 and 186.2 mm³ at that registration. A new approach reference and two guided gates are under test.
From the projected decision pose the empty cassette lowers to −18°. Current rigid stock and five peers clear for 13.54 s to PARK with 10.46 s spare.
Solo score and solo hang are selected. A partner placement and overhead entry pose would require separate evidence.

fixtureSource.scope: Named blue field structure and target hardware; selected minor fixtures and hardware omitted from display. Field contact uses the original separate physics surfaces.

field.status: Preliminary design held · six-NOTE repeatability and ONSTAGE
field.focus: Profile A remains the pickup baseline. Compare R08 before and after seat confirmation, the rejected inward swing, the guided climb and the PARK fallback.
notes: Mesh and beam estimates use the latest staged geometry. Grip, wear, deflection and assembly tolerances require physical measurements.

objectives.objective: Acquire and retain a loose floor NOTE
objectives.basis: Two passive floor followers maintained the tested pickup band across 72 parameter combinations. Actual carpet, wheel wear and arm loading need calibration.

objectives.objective: Score six distinct floor NOTES in 120 seconds on 19 of 20 frozen starts
objectives.basis: Two failed setups in the frozen twenty-start roster. R01 missed the paired counters; R08 never seated the third NOTE. The maximum is 18 of 20 against a target of 19.

objectives.objective: Turn and raise while carrying; recover or reset for the next pickup
objectives.basis: The floor NOTE stayed in the cassette through the commanded swing and slide at both resolutions. Traversal under chassis acceleration and yaw is open.

The original inward swing hits a fixed stage rail. Both simulated CG extremes lifted on the 220 mm guided pull. The adverse hold had only 4.8 mm floor clearance against the 10 mm design allowance. The provisional carriage exceeds the mass margin by 551 g.
The revised east-side route takes 12.61 s and places the bumper 43.3 mm inside. The five terminal-snapshot peers were included.
Solo score and solo hang are selected. A partner placement and overhead entry pose would require separate evidence.

field.validationText: The original inward climb intersects the official fixed stage rail. PARK clears the tested approach. Six of eight frozen scoring starts passed; two failures ended the 19-of-20 campaign. Seat recovery is a separate bounded trial.

objectives.objective: Acquire and retain a loose floor NOTE
objectives.basis: Two passive floor followers maintained the tested pickup band across 72 parameter combinations. Actual carpet, wheel wear and arm loading need calibration.

objectives.objective: Score six distinct floor NOTES in 120 seconds on 19 of 20 frozen starts
objectives.basis: Two failed setups in the frozen twenty-start roster. R01 missed the paired counters; R08 never seated the third NOTE. The maximum is 18 of 20 against a target of 19.

objectives.objective: Turn and raise while carrying; recover or reset for the next pickup
objectives.basis: The floor NOTE stayed in the cassette through the commanded swing and slide at both resolutions. Traversal under chassis acceleration and yaw is open.

objectives.disposition: Both CG trials held after power cut
objectives.basis: The 230 mm guided pull held for five seconds with at least 15.0 mm floor clearance. Battery service, mechanical load and paired cable installation remain open.
The revised east-side route takes 12.61 s and places the bumper 43.3 mm inside. The five terminal-snapshot peers were included.
Solo score and solo hang are selected. A partner placement and overhead entry pose would require separate evidence.

guided.focus: Four of the first five starts produced six individual shot events within 120 s when the field observer kept running. One sixth NOTE reached both beams at 118.264 s. In the remaining start, the third NOTE returned to the carpet. Fifteen starts and the complete shared-counter check remain open.
guided.validationText: 232 occupied solids. Eight internal hoist states and 100 chassis poses screened. Five free-NOTE traces checked. Battery withdrawal at 80° interferes with the right guide. A new −40° service index clears the disconnected battery pull by 5 mm. Physical splice, assembly tolerance and strength are open.
notes: Two chain hooks capture before the shared pivot motor reels. After both slide stops seat, the drive unloads the cable and a passive take-up keeps it tensioned. The spring package is a purchasing allowance.
Scoring replays preserve the original free-piece simulation. The revised mass and inertia still need a matched scoring campaign. Frozen scoring results: six passes, two failures, twelve unrun.
The 55.963 kg upper inspection estimate includes 6 kg of general reserve and 0.20 kg of take-up hardware.

case.basis: Empty cassette supported at −40° with slide and rotation locks engaged, power isolated. Pull the four chassis-side connectors clear, loosen the motor-side shaft clamp at the indexed service clock, release the two cap retainers, then withdraw the bench-assembled motor 45 mm. Connector volumes are reservations at measured motor wire exits.

witness.reason: Reduced head height and two relocated receiver screws clear the full rotating cylinder. The first layout had 56.53 mm³ of hub interference with a receiver screw.
Both 75 mm driver corridors clear at −10°, 0° and +10° about the service clock. At +90° they enter the feed belt and the receiver.
Continuous straight 45 mm removal volume clears the supported robot. The connected-pin control resists a 1 mm sideways pull at all four ports.
Projected peak torque is 0.364 N·m. Clamp grip, real connector fit, cable restraint and the selected screw/nut life still require verification.
